children: The Indonesian rupiah weakened toward IDR 18,040 per U.S. dollar on Thursday, continuing its previous decline amid broad-based dollar strength ahead of next week’s Federal Reserve meeting, where interest rates are widely expected to remain unchanged.
Locally, oil prices around USD 100 per barrel added to fiscal concerns, while a steeper rise in food costs linked to El Niño sustained inflationary pressures.
Sentiment was further dampened by President Prabowo’s criticism of MSCI’s proposed changes to Indonesia’s market classification, deepening worries about potential foreign capital outflows.
Still, Bank Indonesia’s liquidity measures may have helped cushion the decline.
The central bank held its key rate steady for a fourth straight month in October but raised the deposit facility rate by 25bps to 5%.
It also announced reserve requirement cuts for commercial banks, from 9% to 8% from Nov. 1 and to 7% starting Dec. 1, expected to inject around IDR 190 trillion into the banking system.

title: Rupiah Extends Losses as Dollar Strength, Fiscal Risks Weigh
